genericProblem: A generated read endpoint is not a usable read-model consistency mechanism when no real consumer subscribes to its cache, and a locally owned asynchronous read is not safe when its success and failure writes lack a request-generation ownership check.
searchedSurfaces: P5 original roadmap and implementation plan
both generated face clients and RTK endpoint outputs
all platform-admin and operations-admin feature reads that update local state
foundation async-generation primitive and focused tests

counterexamples.reason: Already owns a request generation guard and preserves the previous successful result on page-change failure.
Root session loading already has a request generation guard and is not a list or candidate consumer.
The modal uses an effect cleanup current flag; it is a distinct cancellation pattern rather than an unowned list state write.

findings.finding: The former generic wire query had no generated operation-shaped hook or active consumer, so its tags could not make a feature read model refetch after a write.
A finite set of local list, candidate, and form-constraint reads can write success or failure state after a newer pagination, context, route, or drawer lifecycle has superseded their request.

preventionDispositions.reason: The generated RTK output must contain a request helper and build.query/build.mutation endpoint for every face operation; the self-test removes a helper and must fail.
The P5 implementation review enumerates the finite consumer denominator and requires every retained local asynchronous state writer to prove a current-generation or lifecycle-cancellation owner.
